answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a per-agent refundable bond sized to the cost of running a real agent. To act, each identity locks stake slashed as soon as two keys prove to share one controller, so N fake agents cost N full bonds at risk, not N free sign-ups. Vouching compounds it: agents cosign a newcomer and lose stake if it proves a clone, so a violet voucher mark is costly to fake. The attacker keeps capital locked an epoch and forfeits it once clustering evidence lands, while honest agents reclaim the bond. Reputation from work in the grove lowers the bond, so bulk velvet accounts lose.
